meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Civil Law (French/Italian inspired) with Sharia as principal source of legislation

Arab League Unified Agreement for Investment of Arab Capital in Arab States (1981)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended by Laws No. 36/2014 and No. 154/2019) and its Executive Regulations; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Regulations; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) UBO disclosure rules and GAFI beneficial ownership register guidelines

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each beneficial owner’s valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or Ministry of Interior of the shareholder’s country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a Hague Apostille Convention party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, Register of Directors, or corporate extract of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry or Chamber of Commerce of shareholder’s country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and good-standing letter for each corporate participant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank of account-holding institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for local incorporation agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Retained Egyptian law firm or certified translation office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and Egyptian Ministry of Interior terrorist list; PEP determination using a risk-based approach with enhanced due diligence for senior public officials, their relatives, and close associates, compliant with Article 2 and Articles 6–14 of AML Law No. 80/2002 and CBE AML/CFT regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop (OSS) – Online Company Name Reservation and Commercial Registry portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be registered in Arabic; Latin script is permitted only as a transliteration of the Arabic name. The name must reflect the legal form (LLC/Sh.m.m.), be unique, not misleading, and must not imply any government, military, banking, insurance, or other regulated activity without prior written approval from the competent minister or regulatory authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A company name reservation may be extended for another 30 days by filing an extension request with GAFI before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Grievance Committee within 15 days of receipt of the rejection, attaching a covering memorandum explaining compliance with naming rules and up to two alternative proposed names. The Grievance Committee must issue its decision within 7 business days; an additional judicial review may be brought before the Egyptian Administrative Court within 30 days of the final negative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices offering only postal mail handling are not accepted for LLC registration in Egypt; the company must maintain a physical registered office in Egypt where statutory documents, accounting records, and tax files are kept. Managed serviced/office suites with a fixed physical location may satisfy the requirement, but a P.O. Box address is prohibited. For online e-commerce of maternity and infant care commodities, a dedicated physical office address plus proof of administrative substance (contracts, personnel, or inventory arrangement) is advised in accordance with GAFI and tax authority inspection practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate – estimated 40% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of incorporation for an e-commerce entity, conducted jointly by the Commercial Registry, GAFI, and the Egyptian Tax Authority to verify commercial substance, inventory/logistics records, and statutory record-keeping.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and reservation fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, specifically Articles 20-88 on Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations where investment incentives and non-resident ownership regimes apply; Commercial Registry Law and GAFI one-stop-shop regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Company Registration One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Office at the Ministry of Justice and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (عقد التأسيس والنظام الأساسي) duly authenticated by a public notary and submitted through the GAFI integrated incorporation application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is fixed for LLCs under Law No. 159/1981; the founders determine subscribed capital in the Articles, each share must be fully subscribed, and in-cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank escrow account in the Company's name before notarization; the funds may be released only after the incorporation certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the share subscription schedule in the Articles of Association is ratified; the Manager(s) shall open a licensed bank escrow account, collect the subscribed capital, and hold it in escrow until the registration certificate is issued. (2) That the registered office at Cairo premises designated in the formation file is adopted; the Chairperson is empowered to sign the lease and file the same with the registry authorities. (3) That the individuals named in the incorporation file are appointed as managers/officers for statutory filing purposes. (4) That the Company seal is adopted. (5) That the Chairperson and directors are jointly authorized to complete all GAFI, tax, social insurance, and municipal registrations and to execute ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI — Commercial Name Reservation Desk (online portal gafi.gov.eg and physical one-stop shop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative Arabic or English corporate names for the LLC, indicating the intended activity code (ISIC 4791 - Online Retail Sales). GAFI screens the names against the commercial name database, reserves the first available name, and issues a name reservation certificate to the founders or their authorized representative.
required_dossiers: GAFI Name Reservation Application (Form GAFI-CR-001)
Valid national ID or passport copies of all founders
Notarized power of attorney if a founder is represented by an authorized attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing trademark or corporate name, the founders may file an administrative objection with GAFI within 15 working days or promptly resubmit a revised name application; name reservation fees are not refundable but may be credited to a new reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Public Notary Office (Shahr Aqari notarization desk) or GAFI notarization window within the one-stop shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage licensed Egyptian counsel to draft the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association, including company name, registered office address, directors/managers, share capital breakdown, business purpose, and ISIC activity codes. All foundders or their appointed representatives must appear before the public notary to sign the instrument and authenticate their signatures. Ensure the notary stamps and records the document in the notary register before it is submitted to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Authenticated passport or national ID copies of each founder
Authenticated corporate resolution and certificate of incumbency for corporate founders
Custom-drafted Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name reservation certificate
Proposed lease or preliminary lease contract for the registered office
Founders' declaration of lawful source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial queries for defective power of attorney or non-compliant Arabic provisions are cured by correcting the draft and re-authenticating signatures via the same notary file; the notary may revise the date of attestation without triggering a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Escrow Deposit and Capital Subscription Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian bank with escrow deposit capabilities (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, or a licensed private sector bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital contribution account in the Company's name and deposit the subscribed cash capital from the founders' bank or foreign bank wire transfer. Once funds are cleared, obtain a Capital Deposit Certificate from the bank expressly referencing the Company's proposed name, formation file number, and subscribed capital schedule; the certificate is required by GAFI to prove genuine capitalization.
required_dossiers: Provisional notarized copy of the Articles of Association
Bank account application with authorized signatories
Capital subscription schedule signed by each founder
Proof of remittance for wire transfers from non-resident founders
Company formation number issued by GAFI name reservation desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a certificate with a typographical error or mismatched company name, request a formal corrected certificate within 3 working days; GAFI accepts the rectified certificate so long as the correction is signed by an authorized bank officer and the underlying deposit is unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Integrated GAFI Incorporation Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop — Company Registration Department (integrated submission also covering Commercial Registry and Tax Card signals)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation dossier to the GAFI one-stop shop either electronically or physically; pay the official state fee at the GAFI treasury and obtain a stamped receipt. GAFI reviews legal compliance, verifies the notarized instrument, capital certificate, lease, and identity documents, then issues the Company Incorporation Certificate within the statutory review period. The same integrated file is transmitted automatically to the Commercial Registry and ETA for follow-on registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (three original signed copies)
Bank capital deposit certificate (original)
Notarized lease contract or ownership deed proving premises availability
Valid identification documents for each founder and appointed manager
GAFI integrated registration application (Form GAFI-CR-002)
State fee payment receipt
ISIC activity code declaration (4791 – Online Sales) with NAICS reference for supplementary review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a deficiency query, the founders must cure all missing legalization, attestation, or translation items within 10 working days from notification; if unresolved, the application is administratively deficient and can be reinstated by submitting a fresh integrated application with a renewed fee while retaining the earlier filed priority date where possible.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Tax Authority Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Justice (via GAFI automatic routing) and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the incorporation certificate, the Commercial Registry extracts the commercial registration record and issues the commercial extract; subsequently, ETA issues the provisional Tax Card and the VAT/e-invoice account enrollment. Request the e-invoice signature and QR code activation in ETA's platform, register for withholding taxes, salaries tax, and VAT return filing obligations, and appoint the responsible accountant or tax agent.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate (certified copy)
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Manager's lawful signature specimen and ID copies
Lease contract and premises clearance certificate
ETA tax card application form (Form ET-107)
Bank account certificate showing capital deposit
Board resolution appointing the accountant and tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA or the Commercial Registry flags mismatches in company names, capital records, or activity codes, file a reconciliation letter with GAFI and the registry along with corrected notarized pages; the registration can be amended administratively without court proceedings, and the tax card will be reissued within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Municipal, Civil Defense, and Social Insurance Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Economic Licensing Department (Makan Licensing), Social Insurance Authority (SIA), and the Civil Defense General Administration under the Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the commercial extract and tax card, apply for the municipal economic license covering the office and/or warehouse used for e-commerce fulfillment. Register the founders on contract and any warehouse/administrative employees with SIA for statutory social insurance. Obtain the Civil Defense fire safety certificate for the premises, and complete the workplace occupational health clearance under the Labor Code; integrate payroll for e-payment and e-invoicing.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration extract
Tax card and e-invoice registration confirmation
Lease or ownership title with building code compliance statement
Civil Defense fire safety application and site inspection form
Electrical installation and structural load safety certificates
SIA registration forms for all insurable workers
Municipal economic license application and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority fails to issue the license or the Civil Defense inspection reports defects, remedy the technical deficiencies (additional fire extinguishers, emergency exit signs, corrected load calculations, or enhanced workplace ventilation) and resubmit the file for re-inspection; administrative silence beyond 30 days is contestable via a lawful deemed-approval objection under the Municipal Licensing Law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the General Authority for Industrial Development (GAID) industrial licensing regime is not triggered for ISIC 4791 online retail of maternity and infant supplies; the operative regime is municipal economic licensing of the office and non-manufacturing warehouse under Law 453/1991 and the Commercial Registration Law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Economic License (Rakhasat Al-Manzil / Economic Activity License) for e-commerce retail, customer support office, and warehousing of maternity and infant commodities without manufacturing operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (C) — No EIA required: online retail and dry warehousing are expressly screened out from requiring a full EIA Report or Environmental Registration under EEAA's EIA Classification Guidelines issued under Law 4/1994 as amended by Law 9/2009; the business is exempt from the EIA screening list because it performs no manufacturing, processing, or pollutant discharge activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated; the warehouse must comply with domestic sanitary sewer discharge standards under Law 48/1982 and its Ministerial Decree revisions, including BOD ≤ 300 mg/L and TSS ≤ 350 mg/L for sanitary wastewater only. Solid waste handling must follow the municipal waste management contract and Law 202/2020 on waste management; e-commerce logistics vehicles must meet Egyptian vehicle emission standards under the Clean Air law decrees, and no production-related stack emissions or hazardous waste handling are permitted without a change in industrial classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense fire safety certificate under Law 82/1974 for the office and warehouse, including adequate fire extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke detection, fire alarm systems, and signage; structural load and electrical safety inspection certificates from a licensed engineer under the Building Code (Law 119/2008); and workplace occupational health clearance under the Labor Code Law 12/2003 covering lighting, ventilation, sanitation, first-aid readiness, and employee accident prevention procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt. Official taxpayer portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; e-receipt platform: https://ereceipt.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned LLC registration is completed through the GAFI one-stop-shop (Investor Services Center / Nafeza window): (1) file incorporation documents for the LLC with the Commercial Registry (no statutory minimum capital; foreign ownership is permitted); (2) obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate and publication evidence; (3) register simultaneously with the ETA for corporate income tax (Law 91/2005), payroll and stamp taxes (effective collection via payroll returns), and VAT (Law 67/2016); (4) receive the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and Tax Card; (5) complete mandatory e-invoicing onboarding (SANAD service codes, ETA API credentials or ETA-approved certified service provider) and submit the actual activity commencement declaration. The Tax Card must be issued within 10 business days of complete filing; foreign identity and constitutional documents require apostille and certified Arabic translation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not apply a check-the-box election; an LLC is mandatorily taxable at entity level as a resident juridical person, subject to corporate income tax at 22.5% on worldwide income. Available statutory mechanisms include: (a) fiscal-unity / tax-group treatment for Egyptian subsidiaries held at least 90% (ETA pre-approval required, minimum 3-year commitment); (b) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 threshold; (c) accelerated export VAT refund election under Article 31 bis of the VAT Law for compliant exporters; (d) treaty-based foreign tax credit / unilateral double tax relief election under Article 54 of Law 91/2005; hybrid mismatch consequences follow domestic and MLI rules without an elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations, as amended by Law No. 54 of 2023 (electronic invoicing and fiscal control)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable turnover (mandatory VAT registration threshold for goods and services; voluntary registration permitted below threshold; sectoral service thresholds may be applied by the ETA local branch and should be verified at registration)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance: every VAT-registered LLC issuing B2B or B2G invoices must generate e-invoices in JSON format via the ETA platform or an ETA-approved provider; each invoice receives an ETA-validated UUID, hash and QR code before recognition as a taxable supply. B2C online sellers are phased into the mandatory e-receipt system, under which sales to consumers must be cleared through the ETA in real time. Invoices failing ETA clearance do not support input VAT deduction and trigger administrative penalties (up to EGP 100,000 for first offenders) plus possible suspension of the Tax Card.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to: (i) goods physically exported from Egypt and supported by customs export declarations (VAT Law Article 22); (ii) offshore services supplied to non-residents and fully consumed outside Egypt; and (iii) cross-border e-commerce sales of baby and maternity goods where overseas consumers are invoiced and goods are shipped under the Egyptian customs export procedure. For online sales, export proceeds must be credited to an authorized Egyptian bank account; PayPal/Stripe settlement amounts onward-transferred into Egypt are acceptable if the bank certificate identifies the foreign sales. Deliveries into the Suez Canal Economic Zone (outside customs territory) are equally zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (C24) / Electronic Export Certificate issued by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of goods from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank currency certificate or SWIFT MT103) evidencing foreign currency credited to an Egyptian authorized bank
Commercial invoice, proof of the cross-border sales contract, and e-commerce platform / fulfillment carrier reports matching customer remittances to shipped orders
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and the Central Bank of Egypt systems cross-check export declarations, e-invoices, customs data and foreign currency receipts. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days triggers reversal of zero-rating to 14% VAT, disallowance of input VAT credits, statutory late-payment interest (approximately 14% per annum), and administrative fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000. Fraudulent export claims involving fictitious shipments or forged certifications additionally attract double the evaded tax, imprisonment, freezing of bank accounts, and suspension of the Tax Card pursuant to Law 67/2016 Articles 37, 42 and 44.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), established and governed by Law No. 194 of 2020 (the Central Bank and Banking System Law). The CBE is the sole monetary, banking, and foreign-exchange supervisory authority; its General Administration for Foreign Exchange, the Licensing Department, and the Dealing System Section administer the unified Egyptian foreign-exchange regime, the licensing of authorized dealers, the balance-of-payments classification of cross-border payments, and the foreign-direct-investment (FDI) registration system for capital inflows and repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since 6 March 2024, the CBE has operated a fully liberalized, market-determined exchange-rate regime, and the Egyptian Pound is effectively convertible for current-account transactions. Bona fide trade payments, service payments, and profit/dividend remittances can be executed through licensed banks at the free interbank rate without prior CBE approval, subject only to documentary verification. Capital-account transactions, including equity contributions, intercompany loans, and portfolio inflows, remain regulated: they must be registered with the participating bank under the CBE dealing system and matched against the original inward transfer to support future conversion and repatriation. Repatriation of profits by the EG LLC is legally guaranteed by Article 131 of Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, but remitting banks require (i) the audited financial statements for the fiscal year concerned, (ii) an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax clearance certificate showing full settlement of corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax for the profit year, (iii) a verified capital registration certificate matching the original inbound FDI flows, and (iv) confirmation that no outstanding domestic credit is being financed by the same profits. Practical hurdles are documentary and timing-based rather than blocking: conversion requests are queued at the bank treasury, the beneficiary and the ultimate shareholder must pass sanctions and AML screening, and the LLC must demonstrate that its outstanding local bank borrowings do not exceed the net asset position supporting the distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE's unified foreign-exchange instructions, including the circulars issued contemporaneously with the 6 March 2024 exchange-rate liberalization, export proceeds from the LLC's maternity and infant commodity sales must be repatriated to a licensed Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the on-board date of the bill of lading or the airway bill; service export receipts must be received within 90 days from the invoice date. CBE-authorized extensions of up to a further 90 days may be granted for justified commercial causes, and the full amount of proceeds must be credited to the exporter's foreign-currency account (FCA) at a licensed bank. The statutory mandatory conversion ratio has been abolished: exporters are no longer required to sell a fixed percentage (historically 25-50%) of their proceeds; the LLC may retain 100% of repatriated export receipts in an FCA and convert to EGP at the free interbank market rate at its sole discretion. To certify compliance, the bank requires the export customs declaration filed through the Egyptian Single External Trade Window, the underlying sales contract and commercial invoice, the transport document, and the FX settlement advice; failure to repatriate within the 90-day prescription exposes the LLC to CBE reporting as a foreign-exchange violation, bank-level facility suspension, and statutory penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for share-capital deposit certificate and Operational EGP/FCY Current Accounts (USD and EUR)
Capital Escrow Account for incorporation capital and Operational EGP/FCY Current Accounts, including a dedicated Digital Commerce Gateway partner program
Capital Escrow Account and Operational EGP/FCY Current Accounts with integrated trade finance and online treasury portal
Operational EGP/USD/EUR Current Accounts, Global View Liquidity structure, and non-resident owner onboarding support through the HSBC Global Banking network
Operational multicurrency Current Accounts (EGP, USD, EUR) and documentary credit facilities for import and export settlements
Operational EGP and FCY Current Accounts and trade service desks for open-account and letter-of-credit flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for any CBE-regulated clearing or settlement function in Egypt. Stripe does not operate in Egypt and cannot settle EGP to an Egyptian merchant; PayPal does not provide Egyptian-registered business merchant receiving accounts that credit EGP, and historical PayPal access for Egypt is limited to personal send-side functions. Cross-border digital EMI platforms such as Payoneer and Wise are not licensed by the CBE as foreign-exchange dealers or payment processors in Egypt; they can function only as a pre-collection B2C 'wallet' for the maternity-supplies e-commerce business, with funds subsequently repatriated by SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's Egyptian FCA. The controlling legal constraints are Article 213 of the CBE Law (exclusivity of licensed banks and exchange companies for foreign-exchange dealing), the unified payment-system regulations restricting unlicensed processors from maintaining EGP settlement accounts, and the CBE's anti-money-laundering circulars requiring resident exporters to settle export receipts through a licensed Egyptian bank within the statutory 90-day window.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBE Know-Your-Customer and AML rules, derived from Law No. 194 of 2020 and Law No. 80 of 2002, still require an in-branch identification interview at account opening for at least one director or the legally appointed local compliance signatory. Egyptian-resident directors and authorized signatories must appear physically, present original national ID or valid passport, and execute the account mandate in person. Non-resident directors and shareholders are not generally permitted to open the entity account fully remotely: they may be identified through apostilled or consular-legalized passport copies, notarized board resolutions, and a certified shareholder register, and some banks accept a supplementary audio-video KYC interview for the non-resident beneficial owner, but the final account activation is conditional on an Egyptian-attested verification by the local director or a licensed auditor acting as introducer. Remote-only account opening is not the market standard and is accepted only selectively for the non-resident UBO layer, never for the local operating mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure: overseas shareholders control the Egyptian LLC while the local directors appear only as nominee managers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated UBO declaration signed by every natural-person shareholder; apostilled certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents of the foreign parent; notarized board resolution of the foreign shareholder authorizing the EG LLC opening; passport copies certified by the Egyptian consulate or apostilled; a local auditor's introducer letter confirming the identity and source of funds of each UBO; and a copy of the CBE FDI capital registration established against the inbound share-capital wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Repatriation of export proceeds reaching the onshore FCA after the CBE 90-day statutory window, creating an apparent foreign-exchange violation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sales contracts with Incoterms and payment-term clauses; complete shipping sets including bill of lading or airway bill; Egyptian export customs declarations filed via the Single External Trade Window; commercial invoices matched to the bank settlement schedule; the client's receiving-bank/procurement e-mail log for proceeds status; and a board-approved FX repatriation compliance calendar evidencing follow-up within the 90-day limit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-ticket B2C e-commerce collections with high refund and chargeback volumes settled through third-country PSP wallets rather than direct banking channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated PSP settlement reconciliation reports mapping each Stripe/PayPal/Payoneer deposit to customer orders; payout statements of each electronic money institution; a structured chargeback and refund register; CRM order-level data matching payment identity to delivery status; the bank-approved transaction-monitoring override thresholds for speed-of-transaction anomalies; and the company's e-commerce commercial model description demonstrating that low average ticket value is inherent to maternity and baby supplies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Affiliation of the treasury structure with unlicensed payment processors whose corporate group and ultimate ownership are not fully transparent to the Egyptian bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written PSP notification letter to the bank with a complete compliance pack for each processor, including the processor's applicable license, UBO list, PCI-DSS certificate, and the merchant identification number; a signed undertaking by the LLC to keep PSP balances below the applicable USD/EUR reporting threshold and to repatriate all balances to the Egyptian FCA at least monthly; and bank statements evidencing that PSP wallet balances are used exclusively as pass-through settlement assets, not as offshore treasury stores.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Possible association with cryptocurrency, stablecoin conversion, or informal trade settlement rails detected through payment-narration scans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A crypto-free declaration signed by the beneficial owners and local directors; a compliance manual policy prohibiting virtual-asset invoicing and third-party trade settlement; complete bank-to-bank wire evidence for every import disbursement; transaction surveillance logs from the PSP accounts showing no synthetic or asset-backed settlement tokens; and annual external audit confirmation that all sales revenue is traceable to documented bank or licensed-PSP inflows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital from the non-resident shareholder must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank cover) in USD or EUR to the LLC's designated capital-escrow account at the chosen Egyptian bank, before the bank issues the capital deposit certificate under the Egyptian Companies Law. The incoming wire must carry the standard International Banking Transaction message fields identifying the ultimate originator, the sending bank, and a precise narration referencing the entity ('EG__EG__EG_LLC'), the Egyptian Commercial Registration number, and the phrase 'Share Capital Subscription - Foreign Direct Investment Equity'. The bank will map the transfer to the Egyptian balance-of-payments classification code for foreign direct investment in Egypt - equity capital, register the inflow in the CBE dealing system, and issue an FDI registration and repatriation-rights certificate enabling future dividend and liquidation remittances. The documentary package must include the notarized Articles of Association, the foreign shareholder's board resolution approving the contribution, a legal opinion confirming unlawful incorporation, and proof of authorization of the account signatories; once the subscription is paid, the capital escrow account is converted by bank mandate to the LLC's operational EGP/FCY account, and the capital deposit certificate is stamped and replaced by free-use current accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import settlements covering maternity and infant commodities from overseas suppliers, the LLC will use two primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account and advance-payment structures, and (ii) irrevocable, confirmed documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) for larger purchase orders where the Egyptian bank issues the credit and the beneficiary bank confirms at sight or usance terms. Prior to each outward conversion, the Egyptian bank will require the signed import contract or pro-forma invoice, the final commercial invoice, the NAFEZA Advance Cargo Information Declaration (ACID) number for sea and air cargo, and, after arrival, the customs import release documentation; for L/C disbursements, the bank will process compliance-checks of the shipping documents, including the transport document, insurance certificate, weight/survey certificates, and the LLC's valid tax registration certificate. Export clearing in the same framework is documented through the Egyptian Single External Trade Window electronic export declarations, and all cross-border transactions settle via the bank's nostro/vostro rails with interbank USD/EGP and EUR/EGP pricing, thus keeping the entire liquidity cycle within CBE supervised channels and avoiding secondary unlicensed clearers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (USD/EGP) with tenors matched to the underlying export or import cycle, normally up to six months, executed under the bank's global foreign-exchange master agreement or the standard Egyptian Banking Institute forward terms.
Foreign-exchange swaps combining a spot USD/EGP trade with a matched forward leg, used to manage timing mismatches between import payables and expected export receipts.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR against EGP) for term-alignment of intercompany funding and trade-finance repayments, permitted only where matched with documented commercial debt-service cash flows.

Plain-vanilla OTC currency options (USD/EGP call and put options) purchased for protection on confirmed purchase orders and contemplated capital expenditures, with option premia settled by bank wire and embedded in a board-approved hedging policy.

Collateralized margin-based FX hedging contracts for genuine export-import positions, consistent with CBE margin-trading regulations for commercial end-users; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), cryptocurrency-linked derivatives, and speculative uncovered leverage are not permissible for onshore Egyptian residents.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a late penalty of approximately EGP 500 per month and may result in temporary suspension of the commercial registration record; continued non-renewal for one full calendar year can trigger administrative deregistration of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before 30 April following the close of the calendar-based fiscal year, or within four months of a different fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 500 plus a monthly delay penalty of 2% on unpaid corporate tax; consistent non-filing can lead to collection measures, asset seizures, and criminal prosecution under Law No. 91 of 2005.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the annual shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements, and as part of the GAFI annual update cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update and confirm beneficial ownership may result in administrative fines under the Egyptian AML and investment legal framework, and can prevent the company from requesting official extracts, licenses, or GAFI attestations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC is statutorily required to appoint and retain at least one certified public accountant as external auditor when its issued share capital exceeds EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,030). In addition, the Egyptian Tax Authority requires audited financial statements to accompany the annual corporate tax return for taxpayers whose annual gross revenues exceed EGP 20 million (approx. USD 412,000); smaller LLCs may file unaudited statements unless the shareholders resolve otherwise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are converged with IFRS for most recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a current register of beneficial owners at its registered office and file an annual confirmation with GAFI after the shareholders' meeting. This confirmation must update any changes to shareholding percentages, indirect control links, and individuals holding more than 25% ownership or control. Changes occurring during the year must be recorded within 15 days of the relevant transfer transaction.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year for a compliant registered office or local agent address in Cairo or Alexandria
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - 3,000 per year for a certified audit of a retail e-commerce LLC with standard annual revenues

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% standard CIT rate for resident companies under Law No. 91 of 2005 (Art. 8), as amended by Law No. 6 of 2020; 40% statutory rate applies only to banks, petroleum exploration, and Suez Canal activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME presumptive tax regime under Law No. 152 of 2020: qualifying small e-commerce traders may elect taxation at 0.5%–3% of gross revenue (turnover ceilings per ETA schedules) instead of the 22.5% net-income basis; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 allows 30%–50% deductions from investment costs for qualifying activities; export-oriented projects in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) may access CIT reductions or exemptions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return – Form No. 19, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at incometax.gov.eg; online merchants must also integrate ETA e-invoice and e-receipt systems before filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with four quarterly advance payment installments under Art. 74 Law 91/2005.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Form No. 19 must be filed on or before the end of the fourth month following the fiscal year-end (Art. 73 Law 91/2005); e.g., 30 April for a 31 December year-end. Quarterly advance installments are due within one month after each quarter-end (April, July, October, and January).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, ETA tax card number (TIN), commercial registration number, address, and e-mail of the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Egyptian LLC and its licensed local tax agent are recognized; no foreign parent data is entered in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year commencement and end dates, matching the audited financial statements exactly.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned LLC must file for a full 12-month period; short-period returns arise only on incorporation or cessation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ETA/ISIC activity classification code for ISIC 4791 (online retail of maternity and baby commodities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: E-commerce code must be pre-approved by ETA; misclassification triggers automatic risk-scoring and audit selection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax per the audited income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All deposits from Stripe, PayPal, and local payment gateways must reconcile to recorded revenue; unreconciled PSP deposits are treated as undeclared income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses (Art. 49 Law 91/2005), removal of exempt income, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, royalties, or interest paid to foreign affiliates must be arm's length and supported by documentation to be deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year accepted tax losses, limited to five consecutive years following the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is allowed only against Egyptian-source taxable income of the same business activity; foreign losses are not recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after legal adjustments and loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Law 152/2020 SME presumptive regime is elected, an SME income declaration replaces the full net-income computation; the election is submitted to the ETA before filing Form No. 19.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at 22.5% (or SME presumptive rate), reduced by quarterly advance installments paid, withholding tax credits, and prepayment certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net balance due is paid in EGP; any refund is payable to the Egyptian LLC, not to the foreign parent, and later repatriation is subject to dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Art. 133 Law 91/2005: fixed fine of EGP 10,000–50,000 for failure to file or for incorrect filing; Art. 134: monthly surcharge of 2% on the unpaid tax balance; under-declaration of e-commerce revenue triggers a delinquency penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax; repeated non-filing leads to enforced collection, asset seizure, and ETA audit closure of the online store.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed by a resident Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders (Art. 111 Law 91/2005); the rate is applied to gross distributions without deduction at the corporate level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority; (ii) provide a signed beneficial ownership declaration; and (iii) submit the TRC and treaty relief application to the ETA before the dividend payment date. The Egyptian LLC as withholding agent must obtain prior ETA approval to apply the treaty rate and must retain the approved file for at least five years; treaty relief is denied for shell shareholders without substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under Art. 112 Law 91/2005: 20% withholding tax on royalties and 20% on interest paid to non-residents (also applies to technical service fees). Under Egypt's double tax treaties, rates are typically reduced to 10%–15% for royalties and 10%–15% for interest, conditional on the same TRC/beneficial ownership approval protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million in aggregate related-party/controlled transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory preparation and submission of the Master File, Local File, and the annual transfer pricing disclosure form (Ministerial Decree No. 547/2020 and ETA TP Guidelines); multinational groups with consolidated revenue of EGP 20 billion or more must additionally file a Country-by-Country Report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not impose a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to the UAE regime; however, the ETA applies general anti-avoidance rules, substance-over-form doctrine, and the OECD BEPS beneficial-ownership test. A non-resident-owned LLC without premises, employees, board activity, or fulfilment operations in Egypt is recharacterized as a shell; treaty and investment-law benefits are then revoked and payments reclassified as taxable Egyptian-source income at full statutory rates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting or under-recording online sales settled via Stripe, PayPal, or local payment gateways; maintaining dual bookkeeping sets; destroying point-of-sale invoices or e-receipt records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of EGP 10,000–50,000 under Art. 129 Law 91/2005; civil penalty of 200% of the evaded tax; e-invoice/e-receipt violations carry additional fines up to EGP 50,000; enforced asset seizure and court-ordered closure of the online storefront.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general manager are jointly and severally liable for the LLC's tax debts where default arises from their fault; the ETA may impose travel bans, freeze personal bank accounts, and refer culpable directors for criminal prosecution leading to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC as a letterbox conduit: no physical office in Egypt, no employees, foreign-controlled management decisions, and no local inventory or fulfilment capacity for maternity-supplies e-commerce sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty relief, refusal of Investment Law incentives, and revocation of SME regime eligibility; recharacterization of cross-border payments as taxable Egyptian-source income; reassessment at 22.5% CIT plus 10%–20% withholding and 200% delinquency penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false substance declarations commit a false-affidavit offence; civil restitution of the evaded taxes, personal travel bans, disqualification from management of Egyptian entities, and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or file the Master File, Local File, and annual TP disclosure when controlled transactions exceed EGP 10 million; pricing management fees, royalties, or goods imports away from arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EGP 100,000 for documentation failure under Art. 133 as applied through TP regulations; discretionary TP adjustment to arm's-length income; assessed underpayment accrues monthly surcharges of 2% plus interest on the principal underpayment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false TP computations are jointly liable for the additional tax and interest; submission of forged TP benchmark studies triggers criminal proceedings and personal imprisonment for fraud against the ETA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Non-Compliance and Unlicensed Payment Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Stripe/PayPal payout rails without proper corporate registration with the Central Bank of Egypt and commercial registry; commingling personal and corporate PSP accounts; failing to maintain customer due-diligence and suspicious-transaction records for online sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and licence suspension under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and Central Bank regulations; freezing of PSP and bank balances; criminal forfeiture of proceeds where funds are linked to tax evasion, money laundering, or illegal digital-commerce activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally obligated to report suspicious transactions; failure to do so carries imprisonment of 3–7 years, personal fines, and permanent disqualification from serving as directors or managers of any Egyptian company.
